final_message:
I fixed the bug: `BillingEngine.refund` in `billing/engine.py` passed its arguments to `refunds.refund_invoice` in the wrong order.

The function is defined as `refund_invoice(ctx, invoice_id, reason)`, but the engine called it as `(invoice_id, self.ctx, reason)`. The invoice ID string ended up where the context belongs, which caused `'str' object has no attribute 'store'`. I swapped the arguments back.

I ran your reproduction test as a temporary file. It passed, along with the existing tests (25 passed). I then deleted the temporary file, so the test isn't in the suite.

I wrote `answer.json` as `{"file": "engine.py", "function": "refund"}`. It doesn't show up in `git status`, so it may be gitignored.

steps.command: cd billing && ls && cat reports.py && grep -n "def refund" -A40 engine.py

cd .. && sed -i 's/refunds.refund_invoice(invoice_id, self.ctx, reason)/refunds.refund_invoice(self.ctx, invoice_id, reason)/' billing/engine.py && echo '{"file": "engine.py", "function": "refund"}' > answer.json && cat >> tests/test_reports.py <<'EOF'
EOF
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5; git status --short

echo '{"file": "engine.py", "function": "refund"}' > answer.json
cat > /tmp/t.py <<'EOF'
from billing import reports
def test_x(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    world.engine.refund(inv["id"])
    assert reports.revenue_between(world.ctx, inv["paid_at"], inv["paid_at"] + 1) == {"usd": 0}
EOF
cp /tmp/t.py tests/test_tmp_repro.py; .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -8; rm tests/test_tmp_repro.py; git status --short
